findings.issue_text: [BUG] The new override code calls dayjs(...).tz(...) on the dayjs instance in packages/lib/slots.ts, which only works if the dayjs timezone plugin has been extended in that module — if the module (and its transitive imports) never calls dayjs.extend(timezone), .tz is undefined and every getSlots call with activeOverrides throws TypeError: dayjs(...).tz is not a function. Any schedule request for an event type that has date overrides crashes the slot computation entirely instead of returning a schedule; the very test added in this diff (getSchedule.test.ts override-with-different-timezone case) exercises this path, so CI only passes if the plugin is in fact registered somewhere — which must be verified against the repo, not assumed.

[BUG] The condition `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct dayjs object instances with ===, which is always false, so the intended 'zero-length override' early return never fires. A zero-length (start==end) date override never causes the early return; evaluation falls through to the slotEndTime/slotStartTime comparisons, whose behavior for a zero-length override is untested and does not match the author's stated intent.

[BUG] In the working-hours fallback check, `end` is computed from `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` instead of the slot end time, making `end` identical to `start` and the `end > workingHour.endTime` half of the bounds test dead code. A slot whose start is inside working hours but whose end extends past workingHour.endTime (e.g. a 60-minute booking starting 30 minutes before close) passes the working-hours check and is offered, because the end bound is never actually evaluated against the real slot end.

[BUG] `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` passes availability.timeZone, which is nullable in the Prisma schema, straight into .tz(); a null/undefined timeZone produces a dayjs object with invalid timezone and utcOffset() of 0 (or throws, depending on plugin version), silently or catastrophically corrupting the offset arithmetic. For users whose Availability.timeZone is null (falling back to the default), the organizer offset is computed as 0 while the invitee offset is real, producing overrides shifted by the invitee's full offset — slots appear at wrong local times, and in plugin versions where .tz(null) throws, getSlots crashes for that request.

[BUG] When a date override exists for the slot's day, checkIfIsAvailable returns true immediately via `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;`, bypassing the busy-time check entirely. Any slot falling on a date-override day is returned as available without consulting `busy`, so slots overlapping existing bookings are offered and double-booking occurs on override days.

[BUG] In the workingHours rejection block, `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` duplicates the start computation instead of using slotEndTime, so `end > workingHour.endTime` compares the slot's start minute against the working-hour end. A slot whose start is within working hours but whose end extends past the last working-hour end (e.g. a 60-minute event starting at the final hour boundary) is incorrectly rejected as outside working hours; the slot-end boundary is never actually checked.

[BUG] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two dayjs object instances with ===, which is always false. Zero-length overrides (start === end) are never detected, so the intended 'override with no availability rejects all slots' case falls through to the other comparisons and zero-length overrides leak the day's normal working hours instead of blocking the day.

[BUG] The workingHours find returns true (outside working hours) if the slot start is before ANY same-day workingHour block's startTime, rather than checking containment across the union of blocks. With split working hours on one day (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17), a 10:00 slot is rejected because 600 < 780 for the second block, even though it falls inside the first block — valid slots disappear.

[BUG] checkIfIsAvailable applies a single organizerTimeZone to every dateOverride, but the dateOverrides passed in (built at lines 408-415) carry per-user `timeZone` values that are ignored. For team/round-robin event types with hosts in different timezones, each host's override is day-matched using the organizer's timezone instead of its own, so overrides are matched to the wrong UTC day and slots are wrongly offered or withheld on override days.

[BUG] `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` uses the server's local timezone when `override.timeZone` is undefined, and parsing `Date.toString()` via dayjs is locale/server-dependent. On hosts running in UTC while overrides were defined in another timezone (or where availability.timeZone is null), the computed organizerUtcOffset is wrong, shifting override working hours by the offset difference and producing incorrect slot times.

[BUG] `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` formats in the server's local timezone while `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` is compared against it, so the day match is done in the server's timezone rather than the invitee/organizer timezone. For servers in UTC serving organizers far from UTC, an override near midnight is matched to the wrong calendar day, causing slots just inside the override window to be rejected or normal-day slots on the override day to be offered.

[ADVISORY] The new ~50 lines of date-override/working-hours rejection logic in checkIfIsAvailable have no direct test coverage; the only added test (apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:787-804) exercises the getSlots override-offset path, not this router-level logic. Regressions in the busy-bypass, zero-length, or day-matching logic above will pass CI; a test pinning that a booked slot on an override day is unavailable would have caught the P1 above.

[BUG] In the new working-hours check, `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so it is a copy-paste bug: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start`. A slot whose start minute falls inside workingHour.startTime..endTime but whose end extends past workingHour.endTime is treated as within working hours; long event types leak slots past the end of the availability window, offering bookable times outside the host's schedule.

[BUG] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct dayjs object references with `===`, which is always false; the intended `.isSame()` comparison makes the start===end special case dead code. A zero-length date override (start equals end) never takes its intended early-return path and instead falls through to the range checks, which then mark the slot unavailable for the wrong reason; the special case the author wrote cannot ever execute.

[BUG] The timezone offset is negated before being applied: `const utcOffset = dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1;` then `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` shifts the UTC instant in the wrong direction (local wall time = UTC + offset, but the code applies UTC − offset). For an organizer in UTC+6 the override's calendar day is computed 12 hours off, so a slot is matched against the wrong date's override: overrides silently fail to apply (or apply to the wrong day) for organizers east or west of UTC, and the checkIfIsAvailable override gating returns wrong availability.

[BUG] When a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot falls inside the override window, the function returns `true` immediately via `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;`, skipping the subsequent busy/booking conflict check entirely. Existing bookings on a date-override day are ignored, so two invitees can book the same slot — a double-booking regression that the pre-diff code (which always ran the busy check) prevented.

[BUG] `dayjs(override.start.toString())` parses `Date.prototype.toString()` output (server-local formatting like "Wed Jan 01 2025 10:00:00 GMT+0000") instead of the Date itself, making the offset computation depend on the server's local timezone and on string parsing of a non-ISO format. On any deployment whose TZ is not UTC, dayjs parses the localized string differently and both organizerUtcOffset and inviteeUtcOffset are computed for the wrong instant, producing wrong override start/end minutes; the result also silently degrades if `override.timeZone` is null/undefined, since dayjs.tz falls back to the host timezone.

[ADVISORY] The same override-timezone conversion concept is implemented twice with different formulas: here as `inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` added to a UTC hour, and in checkIfIsAvailable (trpc slots.ts) as `dayjs.tz(...).utcOffset() * -1` applied to a date match — two hand-maintained, mutually inconsistent offset computations for one invariant. The next person touching override timezone handling must keep both formulas in sync; they already disagree in sign convention, and a fix applied to one site will silently leave the other wrong (as the offset-sign bug in checkIfIsAvailable demonstrates).

[ADVISORY] `userAvailability.find(({ user: { id: userId } }) => userId === slotUserId)` runs inside the per-slot, per-user nested loop, performing a linear scan of userAvailability for every slot and every user. For schedules with many hosts and long date ranges this multiplies an O(n) lookup by slots×users; hoisting a Map of userId→schedule outside the loop removes it, and large event types pay this on every page render of the booking page.

[ADVISORY] The new organizerTimeZone-dependent logic silently degrades to offset 0 (`: 0`) when organizerTimeZone is undefined, and the dateOverrides spread passes `availability.timeZone` which is nullable — no validation or fallback to a computed organizer timezone occurs. A user/availability row with a null timeZone yields UTC-assumed override matching with no error or log, so misconfigured data produces subtly wrong availability that operators cannot detect; a defensive default here also means the sign/conversion bugs above hide rather than fail loudly.

[ADVISORY] The date-override availability check is implemented via `dateOverrides.find()` with a side-effecting `dateOverrideExist` flag and overloaded return semantics (true means "unavailable" in one branch and "within range means available" in another), inside a boolean helper. The next change to this logic must reverse-engineer the three-way implicit contract (find-true → unavailable, flag-set-and-find-false → available, flag-unset → fall through) before making any edit; restructuring into explicit named booleans removes the mutation and the dual-meaning return.

[BUG] The working-hours availability check computes `end` from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, making `end` always identical to `start`. The condition `end > workingHour.endTime` can never fire based on the slot's actual end, so a slot that starts inside working hours but extends beyond `workingHour.endTime` is reported as available, allowing bookings past the end of the working day.

[BUG] The guard `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct dayjs object instances with `===`, which is always false. The intended zero-length/equal-start-and-end override case is dead code; the branch can never trigger, so slots on such an override day fall through to the wrong availability branch instead of being handled as intended.

[BUG] When a date override exists for the slot's day, `checkIfIsAvailable` returns `true` immediately (`if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }`) before ever evaluating the `busy` array. On any day that has a date override, existing bookings (the `busy` list) are ignored entirely, so slots overlapping a confirmed booking on an override day are offered as available — enabling double-booking exactly on override days, the days most likely to be manually curated.

[ADVISORY] The override-day offset in `checkIfIsAvailable` is derived from `organizerTimeZone`, while the parallel offset computation for the same overrides in `packages/lib/slots.ts` (line ~212) is derived from `override.timeZone` (the availability's own timeZone) — two different sources for the same semantic value. When a user's availability timeZone differs from the organizer/eventType/schedule timeZone, the two computations disagree: `getSlots` shifts the override to one day while `checkIfIsAvailable` tests membership on another, so overrides are silently misclassified for multi-host or mismatched-timezone setups.

[ADVISORY] The new `organizerTimeZone` argument is optional and its call sites pass values (`schedule.timeZone`, `userSchedule?.timeZone`) that can be undefined, in which case `checkIfIsAvailable` silently assumes UTC offset 0. For any availability/schedule without a resolvable timeZone, override-day detection computes offsets as 0 and slots on override days are dropped or wrongly kept, with no error signal — a silent wrong-availability failure rather than an explicit configuration gap.

[ADVISORY] A fresh linear `userAvailability.find(...)` is executed inside the per-slot, per-user loop solely to recover `timeZone` that was already attached to the dateOverrides/workingHours data. Adds an O(slots × users × availabilities) scan on the hot slot-generation path; a map keyed by userId built once before the loop would make the lookup O(1) and keep the timezone data with the record that owns it.

[BUG] checkIfIsAvailable computes slotEnd from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime ('const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()'), so the end-of-slot working-hours boundary is never actually checked. A slot whose start is inside working hours but whose end spills past workingHour.endTime is treated as fully inside working hours and returned as bookable, contradicting the function's stated intent of rejecting slots outside working hours.

[BUG] The date-override comparison 'dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset,...) === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset,...)' compares dayjs object references with ===, which is always false. The zero-length-override guard is dead code; zero-length overrides fall through to the range checks and are handled by accidental rather than intended logic, silently deviating from the written intent.

[BUG] The newly added workingHours/dateOverride filtering in checkIfIsAvailable compares slot times in the invitee/request timeZone against workingHours minute values defined in the organizer's reference frame, without converting between them. For invitees in a different timezone than the organizer, valid slots that getSlots already produced via working-hours logic are additionally re-filtered here with mismatched frames and get dropped — existing availability behavior silently changes for cross-timezone bookings with no explicit acceptance of that semantic change.

[BUG] The override conversion reinterprets existing stored dateOverrides: previously they were read as plain UTC hours (getUTCHours), now they are shifted by the difference between the override's timeZone and the request timeZone, changing the meaning of all pre-existing stored overrides without a data migration or explicit sign-off. Every schedule rendered for existing users with date overrides changes (slots appear/disappear depending on invitee timezone), i.e. the accepted behavior of stored overrides is silently redefined by this diff; users with overrides in a different organizer timezone than the request see shifted availability.

[BUG] dateOverrides parameter is declared as { start: Date; end: Date }[] but callers pass objects that also carry userId and timeZone (added in this diff), so the typed contract no longer matches the actual payload. The extra fields are silently discarded by the type system while the function's offset logic relies on organizerTimeZone being passed separately and correctly; any future caller following the declared type gets utcOffset 0 and mis-classifies override days, a latent intent/type drift.

[ADVISORY] organizerTimeZone is now sourced from schedule.timeZone / userSchedule?.timeZone at call sites, duplicating the eventType.timeZone || schedule.timeZone || userAvailability[0].timeZone fallback chain computed at line 439, creating two parallel sources of the same value that can diverge. The per-slot organizerTimeZone (individual availability's timeZone) differs from the loop-level organizerTimeZone (event-level fallback) — the same request uses two different 'organizer timezone' definitions in getSlots vs checkIfIsAvailable, so the next timezone fix must be applied in both places or behavior diverges further.

[ADVISORY] checkIfIsAvailable has grown from a pure busy-conflict predicate into a date-override + working-hours filter with three nested find blocks and side-effecting dateOverrideExist mutation, a structural smell that makes the next availability change risky. The next contributor touching availability must reason about three interacting early-return paths plus a mutable flag set inside a find callback; the mutation-inside-find pattern is easy to break (e.g. reordering conditions flips dateOverrideExist) and already obscured the intent (the dead === comparison).

[BUG] The zero-length-override guard compares two distinct dayjs objects with === (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`), which is always false for objects, so this branch is dead code. A date override with identical start and end never short-circuits via this check; the code falls through to the isBefore/isSame and isAfter checks instead. The intended zero-duration handling silently never executes, and no test in the diff exercises a zero-length override to catch it.

[BUG] In the working-hours check, `end` is computed identically to `start` (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`) — the slot's end time is never computed, so the upper bound check `end > workingHour.endTime` tests the slot start twice. A slot that starts inside working hours but whose duration extends past workingHour.endTime is incorrectly rejected or, more importantly, the endTime bound is meaningless — slots are judged only by their start minute against both bounds. Any test asserting slot end-boundary behavior would fail; none exists in the diff.

[BUG] When a slot falls inside a date override, `dateOverrideExist` is set to true and the function returns true at `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` before the busy-times check ever runs, so bookings during a date override cannot block the slot. A user with an existing booking inside their date-override window still sees that slot offered as available; double-booking becomes possible on override days. Before this change, the busy check ran for every slot.

[ADVISORY] The only test change in the diff is a single positive-path case asserting that slots are present; it never asserts exclusion behavior — no test drives a slot that lies outside a date override, a zero-length override, or a busy booking inside an override through the rewritten checkIfIsAvailable branches. The entirely new date-override/working-hours gating logic in checkIfIsAvailable (trpc/viewer/slots.ts lines 102-160) is exercised only incidentally via the happy path; regressions in the exclusion branches (which contain the two mechanical bugs above) would pass this suite. Test files checked: apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts — the only test-shaped file in the diff; it contains no assertions against checkIfIsAvailable's new branches.

[ADVISORY] Offsets are derived by re-parsing a Date through `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` — a locale-formatted string round-trip — and the same `.utc().add(offset)` expression is evaluated twice per field for hour and minute. The offset source here (override.timeZone, per-availability) is a different mechanism than the router's organizerTimeZone computation (dayjs.tz on the raw Date in checkIfIsAvailable), so the two files can disagree about the organizer's offset for the same override; the toString() parse is also not guaranteed to round-trip identically across environments. Anyone debugging slot shifts has two divergent offset derivations to reconcile.

[ADVISORY] The new organizer-timezone offset math (`dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1`) treats the UTC Date's wall-clock fields as if they were local time in organizerTimeZone and then negates the offset — a sign-flip hack whose semantics differ from the dayjs(...).tz(...).utcOffset() computation in packages/lib/slots.ts for the same overrides. For availability whose timeZone differs from eventType.timeZone/schedule.timeZone (both are fed into organizerTimeZone), the date-override day matching in checkIfIsAvailable and the slot shifting in slots.ts can disagree, producing slots attributed to the wrong override day. The single added test only covers a case the comment asserts should be unchanged, so this divergence is untested.

[BUG] The zero-length-override guard compares two dayjs objects with ===, which is reference equality and always false. dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) never evaluates to true, so a start==end date override (a fully blocked day) is never detected by this branch; the slot then falls through to the range checks where a slot inside the degenerate window is wrongly treated as available, so slots are offered on a day the organizer blocked with an all-day override.

[BUG] The working-hours check computes `end` from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, so end always equals start. `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` duplicates the start computation, making `end > workingHour.endTime` compare the slot's start minute against the workday end; a long booking whose start is inside working hours but whose end extends past them (e.g. 30-minute slot starting 30 min before close) is not filtered out and is offered outside the organizer's working hours.

[BUG] The date-override window math mixes server-local dayjs rendering with a timezone offset derived via dayjs.tz, producing different results on any server whose local timezone is not UTC. `dayjs(date.start)` (line 106, 112, 117) renders the stored UTC Date in the host machine's local timezone, then adds `utcOffset * -1`; on a server running in e.g. America/New_York every shifted boundary is off by the server offset (300 minutes), so the override-day match `format('YYYY MM DD')` and the inside/outside comparisons are wrong and slots on override days are offered or withheld incorrectly. The test suite (UTC CI) cannot catch this.

[BUG] The override offset computation calls .tz(override.timeZone) on a value that is optional and may be undefined, and parses via .toString() which is a deprecated/ambiguous dayjs parse path. TimeRange.timeZone is declared optional in packages/types/schedule.d.ts and is only populated by the getSchedule router path; any caller of getSlots whose overrides lack timeZone (existing consumers, seeded data) passes undefined to dayjs.tz, which resolves to the server's local timezone, giving a wrong organizerUtcOffset; additionally `dayjs(override.start.toString())` parses a locale/zone-formatted string rather than the Date, so the parsed value's offset is environment-dependent and the computed startTime/endTime minutes silently shift for all pre-existing callers that don't set timeZone.

[ADVISORY] When dateOverrideExist is true the function returns true immediately, skipping the busy (existing booking) intersection check entirely. A slot on a date-override day is reported available regardless of existing bookings that overlap it, so the date-override day allows double-booking; anyone relying on checkIfIsAvailable to also consult `busy` for override days gets confirmed-overlapping bookings.

[ADVISORY] The working-hours fallback uses slotStartTime.day()/hour()/minute() in UTC rather than the organizer timezone used for the override check, so the day-of-week match is wrong for organizers whose local day differs from the UTC day. For an organizer in UTC+6 whose working hours are on their local Monday evening (already UTC Tuesday), slotStartTime.day() matches the UTC weekday, so the new out-of-working-hours guard either rejects valid slots or accepts invalid ones for any organizer offset far enough from UTC to cross midnight; the previous behavior delegated day matching to getAggregateWorkingHours input which was built in the right reference frame.

[BUG] When a date override exists for the slot's day, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before the busy-time check, so existing bookings are ignored on override days. On any day with a date override, the `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` branch short-circuits past the `busy.every(...)` check (and the currentSeats seat check has already returned), so slots are offered as available even when the organizer has a calendar booking overlapping them — inviting double bookings that the pre-diff code (busy-only path) prevented.

[BUG] The slot end time in the working-hours check is computed from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`), so `end > workingHour.endTime` can never fire except when the start itself is past closing. A slot that starts inside working hours but ends after them (e.g., a 60-minute slot starting 16:45 against hours ending 17:00, or the last slot of a shorter workingHour interval) passes the outside-working-hours filter and is offered as bookable even though it extends past the organizer's availability.

[BUG] The zero-length-override guard compares two distinct dayjs instances with `===` (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`), which is always false, making the branch dead code. An override whose start equals its end never short-circuits and instead falls through to the before/after window checks; combined with the dateOverrideExist early-return this silently produces 'whole day available' behavior instead of whatever the equality branch was meant to guard, and the comparison reads as intentional logic to future maintainers.

[BUG] In the grouped/fixed-host filter, `userAvailability.find(...)` for slotUserId can return undefined and `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule?.timeZone` then passes undefined, hitting the `organizerTimeZone ? ... : 0` fallback that treats date overrides as UTC. If a userId embedded in slot.userIds is not present in userAvailability (e.g., a host removed or a schedulingType edge), every date override for that slot is day-matched with a 0 offset, so overrides authored in non-UTC timezones are checked against the wrong calendar day and slots are silently dropped or wrongly kept with no error or log.

[ADVISORY] `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` silently falls back to the server-local timezone when override.timeZone is undefined, since TimeRange.timeZone is optional in packages/types/schedule.d.ts. Any call path into getSlots whose dateOverrides were not annotated with timeZone by this diff (getSchedule annotates them, but getSlots has other callers) computes organizer/invitee offsets from the deployment server's TZ, producing different slot windows depending on where the code runs; a regression here surfaces only as subtly wrong availability with no error.

[ADVISORY] The expression `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute")` is fully duplicated for startTime and endTime (four near-identical constructions, plus two offset computations), so start and end offset math are maintained in parallel. The next change to offset handling (e.g., fixing a DST boundary) must be applied in four places within one flatMap; a missed copy yields start and end shifted by different offsets and silently wrong override windows — extract a single `const shifted = dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute")` per override.
